chunks: Abu 'Ali al-Ash'ari narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Aba Ibrahim عليه السلام about a man who commits zina while he has a concubine or a female slave with whom he has intercourse: does the female slave he has count as making him muhsan? He said: “Yes. That is only because he has with him what suffices him against zina.” I said: What if he has a female slave and claims that he does not have intercourse with her? He said: “He is not to be believed.” I said: What if he has a mut'ah wife—does she make him muhsan? He said: “No. That only applies to something permanent that he has with him.”

key_terms.الدَّائِمِ: that which is permanent, in contrast to temporary marriage
key_terms.الزِّنَى: illicit sexual intercourse subject to legal punishment
key_terms.السُّرِّيَّةُ: a concubine kept by a man as a lawful sexual partner
key_terms.الْأَمَةُ: a female slave owned by a man
key_terms.تُحْصِنُهُ: it renders him muhsan, legally fortified through lawful sexual access
key_terms.لَا يُصَدَّقُ: his claim is not accepted as credible
key_terms.يَطَؤُهَا: he has sexual intercourse with her

ai.seo_question: Does a female slave or mut'ah marriage make a man muhsan in the law of zina?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses a legal ruling concerning iḥṣān in cases of zina. Imam Abu Ibrahim عليه السلام explains that ownership of a female slave with whom intercourse is possible establishes iḥṣān because the man possesses a lawful outlet that suffices him from zina, whereas a temporary marriage does not, since the ruling is tied to a permanent arrangement.
